newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik fighters tell U.N. they killed U.N. hostage.
newsitem.headline: Tajik fighters tell U.N. they killed U.N. hostage.

text.p: The U.N. mission in Tajikistan said on Friday Islamic fighter Bakhram Sadirov had told it that his troops had shot dead a U.N. military observer among the group of Russian and western hostages they are holding, but there was no independent confirmation of the killing.

"Yesterday night Bakhram Sadirov contacted us and confirmed that his people had shot dead a military observer," a U.N. mission source told Reuters in the Tajik capital. The source declined to be named or comment.

The hostage crisis started early last week. The armed Islamic group are holding three U.N. observers -- two Swiss and a Ukrainian -- along with four Russian journalists, four staff of the U.N. refugee agency UNHCR and the Tajik security minister, who was seized when he arrived to try to negotiate freedom for those already held.

The Russian journalists held were the first to report the death of a fellow-hostage on Thursday, but it is unclear whether reports they have sent from captivity simply reflect what their captors want them to say.

Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin spoke to Tajik President Imomali Rakhomov on Friday morning about the crisis, Itar-Tass news agency said without giving details. Rakhmonov has said he is prepared to meet the demands of the hostage takers.

Chernomyrdin said after a late-night government meeting on Thursday Russia would take all necessary means to save the lives of Russian and Western hostages in Tajikistan, and added he hoped they would be released by Friday morning.
